samples.summary: The four new YAML `path` gates use exact `==`, but `checks.mjs` deliberately tolerates the `<file>@<ref>` form — so the same run can be "CI" to mark-ready and "not CI" to every workflow gate
samples.evidence: `checks.mjs:62` normalises with `String(r?.path ?? "").split("@")[0] === CI_WORKFLOW_PATH`, and `mark-ready.test.mjs` has a dedicated test ("gate 1 tolerates the @ref suffix a called workflow reports on its path") declaring that form IN RANGE. The workflow expressions added here — agent-review-panel.yml:117 (concurrency) and :166 (gate if), agent-iterate-ci.yml:54, ci-report.yml:56 — all compare with plain `==` against the bare path. For any payload where `workflow_run.path` carries the `@ref` suffix the panel gate, the CI-fix arm and the CI report all evaluate FALSE and skip. That failure is silent: the `gate` job is skipped, so `needs.gate.outputs.managed` is '' and the `stalled` job (`managed == 'true' && review-panel.result == 'skipped'`) never pages. Two copies of one rule that disagree on an input one of them explicitly declares legal.

samples.summary: The whole agent pipeline is now conditioned on `github.event.workflow_run.path`, a payload field nothing in the repo previously read and nothing validates — an empty/absent value disables panel, fixer and CI report with no page
samples.evidence: `grep` over `.github/` shows `github.event.workflow_run.path` appears only in the lines this diff adds (agent-review-panel.yml:117,166; agent-iterate-ci.yml:54; ci-report.yml:56); it is a first use. The tests exercise the clause only against synthetic PATH values injected into `new Function` (checks.test.mjs:183-218), never against a real payload. If the field is ever missing or differently populated (e.g. for the `requested` action, or a run created before a rename), the expression is false everywhere at once: the panel gate skips, the concurrency suffix resolves to 'noop', `stalled` is gated on `gate.outputs.managed` and therefore also skips, and no human is told. A single unverified field with a fail-silent blast radius over the whole loop.
searchedFor: grep for prior uses of workflow_run payload fields in workflows

samples.summary: The rewritten gate-1 header says "EVERY run of ci.yml ... concluded success", but `ciConclusion` reads only the newest run and ignores older ones
samples.evidence: mark-ready.mjs:7 now reads "1. EVERY run of `.github/workflows/ci.yml` for the PR head SHA concluded `success`". The implementation at mark-ready.mjs:138 is `ciConclusion(data.workflow_runs) === "success"`, and checks.mjs:90-94 takes `newestRun(ciRunsFor(...))` and returns success/failure from that ONE run — checks.mjs:77-84 explicitly records that the every-run variant was reverted. The two files now document opposite rules for the same gate, and the mark-ready text overstates the guarantee a reader of the ready gate is relying on.

samples.summary: `ciRunToRerun` (newest COMPLETED) and `ciConclusion` (newest run, completed or not) can pick different runs, so the re-run's stated justification — "that is the run whose conclusion gate 1 reads" — is false whenever a newer in-flight run exists
samples.evidence: checks.mjs:126-128 filters to `status === 'completed'` before taking the newest; checks.mjs:90-93 does not filter by status at all and returns null when the newest run is unfinished. When a head SHA carries an in-flight run plus an older completed one (a re-opened PR, or a force-push back to a previously-built SHA — both possible under `pull_request`'s default activity types), `@claude rerun`/`@claude loop` re-runs the STALE run. The panel is then admitted on a `completed`/attempt>1 event for a run whose conclusion gate 1 does not read; mark-ready sees the newest (in-flight) run, returns null, and exits 1 — a wasted ~$12 panel round and a PR left a draft while the comment tells the user "the review panel will run again and can promote". The mirrored inline copies at agent-loop.yml:159-160 and agent-rerun.yml:203-204 carry the same divergence.

samples.summary: The new "exactly one CI run per PR head SHA" tripwire only inspects top-level trigger names, so it cannot detect the ways `pull_request` itself already produces a second run for one SHA
samples.evidence: checks.test.mjs:477-482 asserts the event set is exactly `['merge_group','pull_request','push']` and :485-489 that `push` is restricted to main. `ci.yml:9-10` declares `pull_request:` with no `types:`, so the defaults (opened, synchronize, REOPENED) apply: closing and reopening a PR, or force-pushing back onto a SHA that was already built, creates an additional run for the same head SHA. The invariant `ciConclusion`'s doc-comment rests on ("a PR head SHA gets exactly one CI run") therefore does not hold, and the test that is advertised as the tripwire for it would not fire. Newest-wins still returns a defensible answer in those cases, but the guarantee documented at checks.mjs:69-75 and relied on by the reviewer of this gate is overstated.

samples.summary: `newestRun`'s `(r.id ?? 0)` comparison makes id-less runs sort as oldest, so with no ids at all it returns the FIRST element, not the newest
samples.evidence: checks.mjs:97-100: `runs.reduce((newest, r) => ((r.id ?? 0) > (newest.id ?? 0) ? r : newest))`. When every candidate lacks `id` (as in several mark-ready.test fixtures, e.g. okConfig's `workflowRuns` at mark-ready.test.mjs:91 and the two-run fixtures at :189-206 that omit ids), the comparison is always `0 > 0` → false and the first array element wins. The API happens to return newest-first so production is unaffected, but the function silently stops implementing the ordering its comment and the surrounding tests claim, and a fixture without ids can therefore assert the opposite of what it appears to.

verdict.reason: The quoted code exists as described (checks.mjs:62 splits on "@"; the four YAML gates use exact comparisons at agent-review-panel.yml:117 and :166, agent-iterate-ci.yml:54, ci-report.yml:56), but the input the finding depends on cannot occur. The `<file>@<ref>` form of `path` is the called-workflow form (checks.mjs:60; mark-ready.test.mjs:245-247 says the tolerance exists for "the day CI is invoked as a called workflow"), and ci.yml is not callable: its `on:` block is exactly push[main]/pull_request/merge_group with no `workflow_call` (ci.yml:6-28), grep finds no `workflow_call` or local `uses: ./.github/workflows/...` anywhere under .github, and checks.test.mjs:459-490 is a tripwire pinning that exact trigger set. Since only ci.yml can occupy that path and its runs are never called-workflow runs, no workflow_run payload reaching these gates can carry the suffix, so the claimed silent-skip/no-page cascade has no reachable trigger. The two workflow-side copies are additionally pinned against each other across all action/attempt/path combinations by checks.test.mjs:168-219. Remaining concern is future drift if CI ever becomes a reusable workflow — a maintainability issue, and under the correctness rubric an unreachable branch is minor at most, not blocking.

verdict.reason: The clauses exist as quoted, but the finding's premise does not hold. `github.event.workflow_run.path` is not a first, unread, unvalidated field: scripts/agent/checks.mjs:58-62 (`CI_WORKFLOW_PATH` / `ciRunsFor`) already filters run objects on the same `path` field, and mark-ready.mjs:137-138 gates promotion through it — that reliance predates and is independent of the workflow clauses. docs/design/harness-engineering.md:1942-1951 specifies the rule and names exactly these three workflows. The concrete failure mode the reviewer names (typo/rename making the literal unsatisfiable everywhere at once) is guarded loudly: checks.test.mjs:443-454 asserts CI_WORKFLOW_PATH names an existing file whose `name:` is CI (ci.yml:4), and checks.test.mjs:175-218 extracts both the gate `if:` and the concurrency suffix from the YAML and evaluates them against the CI_WORKFLOW_PATH constant across all four action/attempt combinations, asserting they agree and that a real CI path yields `active`/admitted — so a drifted literal fails the suite rather than silently disabling the loop. `path` is a standard property of the workflow_run payload object for every action, and ci.yml is a local file with no `workflow_call` (so no `@ref` suffix form, which checks.mjs:62 tolerates anyway). The `stalled` job's non-firing for refused events is intentional (agent-review-panel.yml:2322-2331 groups it with unmanaged/fork/disabled). The "tests only use synthetic PATH values" half is a test-adequacy point, outside this lens.
